title: Summer 2026 flex burn contingency and pricing coupling
body:
Purpose:
Quick-consolidation spreadsheet to surface near-term hiring triggers, runway delta under pricing shocks, and an ops playbook for a 6–12 week burn compress or stretch. This is intentionally lightweight so ENG/PMs can iterate.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Base assumptions: current committed runway = 13.4 months (as of 2026-06), gross burn = $2.1M/mo, committed HC cost = $1.45M/mo (salaries+taxes+benefits), variable cloud & infra = $420k/mo, opex (rent, tools, sales) = $230k/mo.
- Pricing shock analysis: a sustained -10% effective price realization (mix + discounts) increases net burn by ~$210k/mo and reduces runway by ~2.6 months (all else equal).
- Hiring triggers: implement tiered pause at 1) -5% price realization for 8 weeks, hiring freeze on non-customer-facing roles; 2) -8% for 6 weeks, freeze on all non-essential hires + contractor ramp-down; 3) -12% sustained, immediate cross-functional hiring pause + targeted 10% headcount reduction (scope to be decided).

Table A — month-by-month quick scenarios (compact):
Columns: Month | Net Burn ($k) | Committed HC cost ($k) | Vacant HC (FTE) | Price realization delta | ARR runoff risk % | Runway months remaining
2026-06 | 2100 | 1450 | 12 | 0% | 0.0 | 13.4
2026-07 (base) | 2100 | 1450 | 10 | 0% | 0.0 | 12.9
2026-07 (-5%) | 2310 | 1450 | 10 | -5% | 2.0 | 11.1
2026-07 (-10%) | 2520 | 1450 | 10 | -10% | 4.5 | 10.2
Notes on table: Net Burn = committed HC cost + variable infra + opex + realized pricing delta impact (approx = -price_delta * monthly revenue exposure). ARR runoff risk is estimated probability of churn or new-business slowdown attributable to price compression signals.

Table B — Headcount phasing and role buckets (current plan vs contingency):
Buckets: Eng Infra, Serving Runtime, Product, Sales/Rev, Customer Success, SRE, GTM Ops
Committed FTEs (active): 36 | 28 | 22 | 18 | 12 | 10 | 6
Planned hires Q3-Q4: +18 (mix: 8 Eng, 3 Runtime, 2 SRE, 3 Sales, 2 CS)
Vacant offers / accepted: 6 (4 Eng, 1 Sales, 1 CS)
Contingency priority (if pricing shock triggers):
- Level 1 (-5% sustained 8w): pause offers for Eng infra and non-strategic product hires (save ~ $120k/mo if paused).
- Level 2 (-8% sustained 6w): pause all hiring except critical runtime and customer impact roles; freeze discretionary hiring budget (estimated immediate saving ~ $200k/mo).
- Level 3 (-12% sustained): institute hiring freeze + convert 2 contractor roles to perm re-eval or cancel + targeted reduction (scope to slush list).

Pricing sensitivity matrix (simplified):
- Variable: price realization change vs base (%), impact on net burn ($/mo), impact on 12-month runway (months)
- -3% -> +63k/mo -> -0.8 months
- -5% -> +105k/mo -> -1.3 months
- -8% -> +168k/mo -> -2.1 months
- -10% -> +210k/mo -> -2.6 months
- -15% -> +315k/mo -> -3.9 months
Assumptions: monthly revenue exposure to price changes = $2.1M (rough realized revenue), variable margin pass-through ~100% for sensitivity (conservative).

Operational playbook (quick actionable items):
Immediate (within 7 days):
- Finance to re-run model with latest usage (JIRA-FIN-3421) and confirm realized revenue exposure bucket by customer segment. Owner: Miguel.
- PM/Product: identify 3 features we can temporarily de-prioritize or gate to reduce inference volume (owner: Leah).
- Sales: hold all discretionary pricing promos; escalate enterprise deal pipelines for ARR smoothing (owner: Brian).

If Level 1 triggered (-5% 8 weeks):
- Pause non-critical offers, notify recruiting to slow spend, shift spend to high-impact OT (contractor hours for niche skill where needed).
- Finance to prepare immediate 6-month cash runway reforecast and quick FAQ to execs for comms.

If Level 2 triggered (-8% 6 weeks):
- Pull forward SRE & Runtime hiring only if there's a direct customer SLA risk. Otherwise freeze.
- Begin contractor-to-hire deferral review.
- Ops to evaluate cloud spot/commit mix to squeeze variable infra by up to 15% (target = ~$60k/mo).

If Level 3 triggered (-12% sustained):
- Convene exec review to scope targeted headcount reduction (goal: preserve core serving runtime + customer success where possible).
- Prepare internal comms + legal review for severance scenarios.

Assumptions and caveats (important):
- These numbers are deliberately coarse — this sheet is a working-level tool, not the final pro-forma.
- Revenue exposure calculation uses trailing-3mo average ARR and reported discounting patterns; if a handful of large customers reprice, impact can be non-linear.
- Headcount cost bucket uses loaded cost (salary + payroll + benefits + equity run-rate) at a 1.38x multiplier on salary.
- Cloud savings target assumes ability to shift some steady inference to scheduled batch windows and to implement prefix caching (product+eng effort to enact).

Open questions / action items (TODO):
- [ ] Recon with sales: map top-20 customers' pricing elasticity risk and concentration (due 2026-06-21, owner Brian).
- [ ] Create a small-run experiment to measure prefix caching effectiveness on top-10 high-volume customers (owner: Runtime Eng, due 2026-07-05).
- [ ] Update model to handle non-linear ARR cliff effects (owner: Finance Analyst, due 2026-07-01).
- [ ] Legal + HR ready template for quick pause or reduction comms (owner: Leah).

Appendix (quick calcs):
- Runway months = Cash balance / Net Burn. Example: $28.1M cash / $2.1M burn = 13.4 months.
- Net Burn w/ price delta = base burn + ( -price_delta * revenue_exposure ).
- Hiring saving estimate per paused FTE = average loaded cost per FTE = $12.5k/mo (varies by role).

Notes to reviewer:
- This should be merged with the long-form pro-forma in confluence once validated. Intentionally left in a spreadsheet-friendly layout to drop into Google Sheets.
- Feedback: if we want a second tab with per-customer impact, say so and I'll spin up a draft mapping.

End of sheet — working draft.
